title: Hadith Knowledge
description: Little Muslim → Beginner. Short questions introducing hadith, two familiar collections, careful reporting, simple teachings and everyday examples of putting them into practice. Written with children around ages 6–9 in mind; an adult may read questions aloud. All questions are Beginner level within the Kids audience.
levelMethod: Beginner describes the knowledge and understanding needed across all question styles. Styles are not difficulty levels. Uses introductory hadith knowledge, short wording and straightforward examples for the Kids audience. Age and level are editorial guidance, not calibrated with children's reading or response data. Quiz performance describes learning needs, not a child's faith or worth.

review.referenceCheck: Linked hadith reports and collection introductions checked during preparation. Present-day scenarios illustrate the cited teachings. No question asks children to judge another person’s faith or worth. Questions and explanations are original child-friendly educational paraphrases, not verbatim translations. Everyday scenarios illustrate the cited principles. This is not independent scholarly approval or a completed review with children.

selectionHints.unknownResponse: Use I am not sure as a separate UI action, not a fifth option.

questions.question: What do we call a report about the Prophet's ﷺ words or actions?

options.text: A hadith
A surah
A juz
A rakah

questions.explanation: A hadith can report the Prophet's ﷺ words, actions and what he approved.

questions.question: Which of these is a well-known hadith collection?

options.text: Surah Al-Fatihah
Sahih al-Bukhari
A prayer timetable
A Quran page marker

questions.explanation: Sahih al-Bukhari is a collection of hadith gathered by Imam al-Bukhari.

questions.question: What kind of book is Sahih Muslim?

options.text: A dictionary of plant names
A map book
A hadith collection
A collection of invented adventures

questions.explanation: Sahih Muslim is a well-known collection of hadith gathered by Imam Muslim.

questions.question: When saying that the Prophet ﷺ taught something, what must we avoid?

options.text: Checking the source
Asking a teacher for help
Saying we are unsure when we are unsure
Making up words and calling them his

questions.explanation: We must be honest about the Prophet ﷺ. We must not invent words and call them his sayings.

questions.question: What did the Prophet ﷺ ask listeners to do for people who were absent?

options.text: Pass on his teaching
Hide every lesson forever
Change the message for fun
Only tell people their own inventions

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ asked those who heard his teaching to pass it on to those who were not there.

questions.question: According to the hadith about deeds, what matters along with what we do?

options.text: The color of our clothes
Our intention
How loudly people clap
How expensive our shoes are

questions.explanation: An intention is what we mean to do and why. The hadith teaches that intentions matter.

questions.question: What good should we wish for a fellow Muslim?

options.text: Only things we would dislike
Failure in every good effort
The good we wish for ourselves
Kindness only when we receive a prize

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ taught us to want good for fellow Muslims, as we want good for ourselves.

questions.question: What does the hadith teach us about speaking?

options.text: Say every hurtful thought aloud
Insult people to entertain others
Spread stories we know are false
Say something good or avoid harmful talk

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ taught good speech or silence. We should use words with care.

questions.question: In the hadith about strength, who is truly strong?

options.text: Someone who controls themselves when angry
Someone who always wins fights
Someone who shouts the loudest
Someone who frightens smaller children

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ praised self-control during anger. Strength includes controlling our behavior.

questions.question: Which quality does the hadith say makes things more beautiful?

options.text: Cruelty
Gentleness
Mockery
Rudeness

questions.explanation: The hadith praises gentleness. Treating others gently improves how we behave.

questions.question: Which statement matches the hadith about good deeds and charity?

options.text: Only rich people can ever do good
Kindness matters only when money changes hands
Good deeds can be acts of charity
Helping is worthless without a large gift

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ taught that good deeds are charity. There are ways to do good beyond giving money.

questions.question: Which action does the hadith count as charity?

options.text: Leaving obstacles for people to trip over
Blocking a walkway for fun
Throwing litter where people walk
Removing something harmful from a path

questions.explanation: Removing harm from a path is charity. Children should get an adult's help with anything dangerous.

questions.question: Which good deeds are especially loved by Allah, even when small?

options.text: Those done regularly
Those done only to impress people
Those we only boast about
Those we promise but never attempt

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ praised regular good deeds, even small ones. Little, steady efforts matter.

questions.question: What did the Prophet ﷺ teach about helping people learn religion?

options.text: Make learning needlessly difficult
Make it easier and encourage them
Drive new learners away
Use every mistake to humiliate someone

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ taught ease and encouragement. We can help learners understand without making them feel unwelcome.

questions.question: When asked who most deserved good companionship, whom did the Prophet ﷺ mention first?

options.text: The richest person nearby
The strongest wrestler
The man's mother
The loudest speaker

questions.explanation: He mentioned the mother three times, then the father. The report emphasizes a mother's right to kind treatment.

questions.question: In the hadith about a thirsty dog, which action was rewarded?

options.text: Chasing it for fun
Laughing at its thirst
Keeping all water away from it
Giving the dog water

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ told of a man rewarded for helping a thirsty dog. Caring for animals matters.

questions.question: According to the hadith, what does truthfulness lead toward?

options.text: Goodness and Paradise
Becoming good at deceiving others
Permission to blame innocent people
Freedom to invent any story as fact

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ taught that truthfulness leads toward goodness and Paradise. We practice honesty in everyday life.

questions.question: Which habit does the hadith warn us to avoid?

options.text: Trying to keep a good promise
Deliberately breaking promises
Taking a promise seriously
Being trustworthy

questions.explanation: The hadith warns against breaking promises. We should take good promises seriously and try to keep them.

questions.question: The hadith says Allah looks at which things, rather than our looks or wealth?

options.text: Only our expensive clothes
Only how tall we are
Our hearts and deeds
Only how much money we have

questions.explanation: The hadith points to our hearts and actions. Appearance and money do not decide a person's goodness.

questions.question: What did Jibril repeatedly remind the Prophet ﷺ about?

options.text: Being rude to neighbors
Helping only famous people
Ignoring everyone living nearby
Treating neighbors kindly

questions.explanation: Jibril repeatedly urged kind treatment of neighbors. People living near us deserve consideration.

questions.question: Can a hadith describe what the Prophet ﷺ did, as well as what he said?

options.text: Yes, it can report his actions too
No, only chapter titles count
No, hadith only lists place names
No, it can only describe the weather

questions.explanation: Hadith include reports of his actions as well as his words and approvals.

questions.question: Is Sahih al-Bukhari a surah of the Quran?

options.text: Yes, it is the opening surah
No, it is a collection of hadith
Yes, it is the last surah
Yes, it is another name for Al-Kawthar

questions.explanation: Sahih al-Bukhari collects hadith. A surah is a chapter of the Quran.

questions.question: What can we learn from a hadith collection such as Sahih Muslim?

options.text: The names of every future quiz winner
A new set of Quran chapters
Reports about the Prophet's ﷺ teaching and example
Made-up stories presented as revelation

questions.explanation: Sahih Muslim preserves hadith reports. A teacher can help us understand their meanings.

questions.question: Does a nice-sounding sentence become a hadith just because we like it?

options.text: Yes, any nice sentence is automatically a hadith
Yes, if many children repeat it
Yes, if it has a colorful picture
No, we must check before calling it a hadith

questions.explanation: We must not attach the Prophet's ﷺ name to invented words. Check with a knowledgeable teacher when unsure.

questions.question: Why did the Prophet ﷺ tell listeners to pass on his teaching?

options.text: So people who were absent could learn
So everyone could invent different words
So no one would remember the message
So learning would belong only to one group

questions.explanation: Passing on teaching helps others learn. We should carry the message accurately and explain it with care.

questions.question: What does an intention tell us about an action?

options.text: How heavy their shoes are
Why someone means to do it
Which color they like best
How many people are watching

questions.explanation: An intention concerns our purpose. We try to do good sincerely, to please Allah.

questions.question: Which thought fits wishing for others what we wish for ourselves?

options.text: Only my learning should matter
My friend must fail for me to be happy
I want my classmate to learn well too
No one else should receive kindness

questions.explanation: We can want good learning and kindness for others too. This follows the hadith's lesson of goodwill.

questions.question: Does the lesson about good speech mean we should hide a problem from a trusted adult?

options.text: Yes, silence always means hiding every problem
Yes, no child should ever ask for help
Yes, hurtful secrets must never be reported
No, asking for help can be good speech

questions.explanation: Good speech includes asking for help. Avoiding harmful talk does not mean staying silent when you need support.

questions.question: Does controlling anger mean we can never feel upset?

options.text: No, it means handling our behavior with care
Yes, any upset feeling makes someone worthless
Yes, strong people never have feelings
No, it means we may hurt others when upset

questions.explanation: Feeling upset can happen. The hadith teaches us to control what we do when angry.

questions.question: Which request shows gentleness?

options.text: Help me now, you fool
Please help me when you can
Move, or I will hurt you
You are useless unless you help me

questions.explanation: Gentleness can shape the way we ask for help. Respectful words are better than threats and insults.

questions.question: Can someone without spending money still do an act of charity?

options.text: No, kindness never counts
No, only expensive gifts count
Yes, by doing a good deed
Yes, by taking someone else's money

questions.explanation: The hadith teaches that good deeds are charity. Helping others is one way to do good.

questions.question: Why is removing harm from a walkway a good deed?

options.text: It gives us permission to push people
It makes tripping others acceptable
It means children must handle sharp objects alone
It helps protect people who use it

questions.explanation: Clearing harm helps others use the path safely. Dangerous objects need an adult's help.

questions.question: Which plan best matches the hadith about regular deeds?

options.text: Choose a manageable good deed and keep doing it
Only plan huge deeds we never begin
Do good only when there is an audience
Stop every good habit after one try

questions.explanation: Small, regular deeds build a steady habit. We do our best without taking on more than we can manage.

questions.question: Does making learning easier mean making up religious teachings?

options.text: Yes, change every teaching to suit ourselves
No, explain correctly in a helpful way
Yes, replace learning with invented rules
No, it means never explaining anything

questions.explanation: Ease means helping people learn correctly. Encouragement does not mean inventing or changing the religion.

questions.question: Does giving special care to our mother mean we may be unkind to our father?

options.text: Yes, only one parent deserves kindness
Yes, fathers should always be ignored
No, the hadith mentions the father too
Yes, kindness runs out after one person

questions.explanation: The mother's special right does not remove the father's right. The hadith mentions both parents.

questions.question: What lesson comes from the man giving water to a thirsty dog?

options.text: Only people can ever need care
Animals should be teased when weak
Kindness matters only if the animal belongs to us
Helping an animal can be a rewarded good deed

questions.explanation: The report teaches that caring for animals can bring reward. We help safely and avoid cruelty.

questions.question: Which habit follows the hadith's teaching on truthfulness?

options.text: Keep choosing honest words
Lie whenever a story sounds more exciting
Blame others to avoid every mistake
Call every guess a fact

questions.explanation: Truthfulness grows through honest choices. The hadith encourages us to keep practicing it.

questions.question: What should a good promise mean to us?

options.text: A trick for getting our own way
A commitment we intend to keep
Words that never need any effort
Permission to deceive a friend

questions.explanation: A good promise deserves sincere effort. We should not make promises with a plan to break them.

questions.question: Does wearing costly clothes prove someone has a better heart?

options.text: Yes, expensive clothes prove perfect character
Yes, money always shows who is kindest
No, appearance does not prove a good heart
No, only height proves a good heart

questions.explanation: The hadith directs us to hearts and deeds. We should not judge someone's goodness by their clothes or money.

questions.question: Why should we care about people living near us?

options.text: Only wealthy neighbors deserve respect
Living nearby makes their feelings unimportant
Kindness should stop at our front door
The hadith gives neighbors a right to kind treatment

questions.explanation: The hadith emphasizes neighbors' rights. Care for them is part of our daily conduct.

questions.question: Your teacher shares a checked report of something the Prophet ﷺ did. What kind of report is it?

options.text: A hadith
A Quran surah
A prayer timetable
A made-up adventure

questions.explanation: Reports about the Prophet's ﷺ actions are among the kinds of hadith we learn.

questions.question: You see a book titled Sahih al-Bukhari. Which shelf label fits it?

options.text: Quran surahs
Hadith collections
Maps and atlases
Invented adventures

questions.explanation: Sahih al-Bukhari belongs with hadith collections.

questions.question: A teacher gives you a hadith reference from Sahih Muslim. Which collection should you look in?

options.text: A weather diary
A spelling dictionary
Sahih Muslim
A book of maps

questions.explanation: The reference names Sahih Muslim, so that is the hadith collection to look in.

questions.question: A picture says a sentence is a hadith, but gives no source. What should you do before sharing it as his words?

options.text: Invent a reference number
Assume the pretty design proves it
Repeat it as certain without checking
Ask a knowledgeable teacher to check it

questions.explanation: A picture alone does not prove a saying is a hadith. Ask someone knowledgeable before attributing it to the Prophet ﷺ.

questions.question: You want to share a hadith lesson your teacher explained. What is a good way to do it?

options.text: Check the meaning and pass it on accurately
Add made-up words for excitement
Change it so your friend loses a game
Pretend your own opinion is the Prophet's ﷺ wording

questions.explanation: Pass on what you have learned accurately. Ask your teacher when you are unsure of its meaning or wording.

questions.question: Before helping tidy the classroom, which intention is good?

options.text: To make others feel worthless
To please Allah by doing something helpful
To show everyone that only I matter
To earn a chance to insult someone

questions.explanation: We try to do good sincerely. A good intention can be to please Allah through helping others.

questions.question: You hope to do well in a lesson. What wish for your Muslim friend fits the hadith?

options.text: I hope my friend never understands
I hope nobody helps my friend
I hope my friend learns well too
I hope my friend loses every chance to learn

questions.explanation: Wishing good learning for a friend follows the lesson of wanting good for others as for ourselves.

questions.question: Some children start insulting a classmate. Which response follows the hadith about good speech?

options.text: Add a cruel joke
Spread the insults to another group
Shout an even worse insult
Avoid the insults and speak kindly

questions.explanation: Choose helpful words and avoid hurtful talk. If someone is being bullied, ask a trusted adult for help.

questions.question: You feel angry after losing a game. Which action shows the strength praised in the hadith?

options.text: Pause and avoid hurting anyone
Hit someone to prove you are strong
Throw a game piece at your friend
Shout insults until everyone leaves

questions.explanation: Self-control means handling anger without hurting people. Pause and ask for help calming down if you need it.

questions.question: Your little brother is learning to button his shirt. Which response shows gentleness?

options.text: Call him useless
Offer calm help without mocking him
Pull at his clothes angrily
Laugh until he feels ashamed

questions.explanation: Gentle help follows the hadith's lesson. We can be patient with someone learning a new skill.

questions.question: You have no money to give today. Which action still fits the hadith about good deeds?

options.text: Take a coin from someone else's bag
Mock someone asking for help
Help a classmate find a lost notebook
Refuse kindness because you have no coins

questions.explanation: A helpful good deed can be charity. You do not need money for every kind of giving.

questions.question: You notice broken glass on a walkway. How can you help keep the path safe?

options.text: Pick up the sharp pieces with bare hands
Scatter it farther across the path
Push someone toward it
Tell an adult who can remove it safely

questions.explanation: Removing harmful things is a good deed. With broken glass, get an adult's help instead of handling it yourself.

questions.question: You want a habit that follows the hadith about regular deeds. Which plan fits?

options.text: Do one manageable helpful task each day
Boast about a huge task you never start
Help once only to win applause
Give up every good deed because it seems small

questions.explanation: Choose a small good deed you can maintain. The hadith values steady effort, even when little.

questions.question: A new learner finds a hadith lesson difficult. How can you encourage them?

options.text: Laugh because they are new
Explain a little at a time and offer help
Make the explanation harder on purpose
Say they should never learn again

questions.explanation: A patient, clear explanation helps someone learn. This applies the teaching of ease and encouragement.

questions.question: Your mother asks you to put away your own toys. Which response practices the hadith's lesson of kind companionship?

options.text: Insult her for asking
Make a bigger mess to upset her
Reply respectfully and help
Say kindness is only for friends

questions.explanation: Respectful words and suitable help are ways to show your mother the kindness emphasized in the hadith.

questions.question: With an adult's help, you can put clean water out for thirsty birds. Which choice follows the hadith's lesson?

options.text: Throw stones at the birds
Hide water just to watch them struggle
Chase them for being thirsty
Provide the water safely

questions.explanation: Safely providing water is one way to care for animals, following the lesson of the thirsty-dog report.

questions.question: You forgot your homework. Which answer follows the hadith about truthfulness?

options.text: Admit it honestly and ask how to catch up
Invent an emergency that never happened
Blame a classmate who did nothing
Say you handed it in when you did not

questions.explanation: An honest answer follows the hadith's lesson. Tell the truth and work on putting things right.

questions.question: You promised to return a borrowed book tomorrow. What should you plan to do?

options.text: Hide it and pretend to forget
Return it as promised
Keep it because promises do not matter
Give it away without the owner's permission

questions.explanation: Take the promise seriously and plan to return the book. Keeping good promises helps people trust us.

questions.question: A child has simple clothes and treats others kindly. Which response fits the hadith about hearts and deeds?

options.text: Mock them for having less money
Say costly clothes are proof of kindness
Respect them without judging their clothes
Refuse friendship because their shoes are plain

questions.explanation: The hadith teaches that appearance and wealth do not decide goodness. Treat others with respect.

questions.question: You are playing near a neighbor's door. Which action shows the kind treatment taught in hadith?

options.text: Block their doorway for fun
Throw litter into their yard
Shout insults when they walk past
Keep their entrance clear and avoid disturbing them

questions.explanation: Consider your neighbor's needs while you play. Keeping their entrance clear is one way to show care.
